 JJ Redick gives major Luka Doncic update after new concerning injury 
 2026-10-29 01:40 
 JJ Redick announced that Luka Doncic (back) and Ziaire Williams (foot) woke up with tightness and soreness, respectively, ahead of their Wednesday game against the LA Clippers.
 Credit: Imagn Images - Scanpix 
 Credit Imagn Images - Scanpix 
 Credit Imagn Images - Scanpix

 The Los Angeles Lakers are taking a cautious approach with Luka Doncic after the superstar was ruled out of Wednesday’s game against the LA Clippers due to back tightness.

 Speaking to reporters before the matchup, head coach JJ Redick revealed that Doncic and Ziaire Williams, who is dealing with left foot soreness, both woke up with their respective injuries.
 "Both those guys woke up with some soreness and tightness today. Well, tightness and soreness: tightness for Luka, soreness for Ziaire," Redick said.
 "We have a tough stretch of games, not a lot of time between. Just being overly cautious."
 Luka Doncic, Ziaire Williams out for Lakers vs. Clippers
 The Los Angeles Lakers decided to sideline both Luka Doncic and Ziaire Williams on Wednesday as they will play the second night of their back-to-back slate.
 Doncic played 37 minutes in Tuesday's 136-129 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers, dropping 41 points, five rebounds, and nine assists while shooting 12-of-22 from the field.
 Williams, on his end, dropped 11 points, four assists, two steals, and two rebounds in 29 minutes.
 With Doncic out, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler are expected to lead the Lakers. Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili, and Matisse Thybulle are also needed to step up.
 The Lakers will look to be back on the win column, as they will face the Clippers for the second time this season. They outlasted their crosstown rival last week with a 125-117 win.
 Luka Doncic, Ziaire Williams status vs. Warriors still uncertain
 As such, JJ Redick is noncommittal when asked if both Luka Doncic and Ziaire Williams can suit up for their NBA Cup opener in Golden State against the Warriors.
 "That's the hope," Redick simply told reporters.
